question: What is the HCF of 72 and 120?
why: 72 = 2^3 x 3^2 and 120 = 2^3 x 3 x 5. Common part is 2^3 x 3 = 24.

question: What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
why: 12 = 2^2 x 3 and 18 = 2 x 3^2. Take the highest powers: 2^2 x 3^2 = 36.

why: HCF x LCM = product of the numbers, so LCM = 2400 / 20 = 120.

question: Which is the prime factorisation of 360?
why: 360 = 8 x 9 x 5 = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5. The other products give 600, 540 and 240.

why: Other number = (HCF x LCM) / 60 = 4500 / 60 = 75.

question: Three temple bells ring every 18, 24 and 30 minutes. They ring together at 8:00 a.m. When will they next ring together?

question: For every natural number n, what is the greatest number that always divides n(n + 1)(n + 2)?

why: HCF + 14 HCF = 600 gives HCF = 40 and LCM = 560. Other number = 40 x 560 / 280 = 80.

question: The decimal expansion of 29 / (2^3 x 5^5) terminates after how many decimal places?

question: In proving that root 3 is irrational, we assume root 3 = p/q in lowest terms and reach 3 divides p and 3 divides q. Why is this a contradiction?
a: p and q then share a common factor 3
b: p and q are both even
c: q turns out to be zero

why: Dividend = divisor x quotient + remainder, so g x (x - 2) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 3x - 2 = (x - 2)(x^2 - x + 1). Hence g(x) = x^2 - x + 1.

why: (1/cos A + sin A/cos A)(1 - sin A) = (1 + sin A)(1 - sin A)/cos A = cos^2 A/cos A = cos A.

question: From a point on the ground the angle of elevation of a tower top is 30 degrees. After walking 40 m towards the tower it is 60 degrees. How tall is the tower?

question: From the top of a 30 m building the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a tower are 30 degrees and 60 degrees. How tall is the tower?
why: Distance = 30/tan 60 = 10 root 3. The tower top is 10 root 3 x tan 30 = 10 m below the building top, so the tower is 30 - 10 = 20 m.

question: From a point 40 m from a building the angle of elevation of its top is 45 degrees, and of the top of a flagpole on it is 60 degrees. How long is the flagpole?
why: Building = 40 m. Total height = 40 root 3 m. Flagpole = 40 root 3 - 40.

question: Two poles of equal height stand on opposite sides of a road 80 m wide. From a point on the road between them the angles of elevation of the tops are 30 and 60 degrees. What is the height of each pole?
why: h cot 30 + h cot 60 = 80 gives h(root 3 + 1/root 3) = 80, so h = 20 root 3 m.

question: The angle of depression of a ship from a 100 m lighthouse is 30 degrees. The ship sails towards the lighthouse until the angle of depression becomes 45 degrees. How far has it sailed?
why: Initial distance 100 root 3, new distance 100. Movement = 100(root 3 - 1).

question: A 20 m ladder first makes 45 degrees with the ground and is then moved so it makes 60 degrees. How much higher does it now reach on the wall?
why: Heights are 20 sin 60 = 10 root 3 and 20 sin 45 = 10 root 2. The gain is 10(root 3 - root 2).

question: The shadow of a pole is 20 m shorter when the sun is at 60 degrees elevation than when it is at 30 degrees. How tall is the pole?
why: h cot 30 - h cot 60 = 20 gives h x 2/root 3 = 20, so h = 10 root 3 m.

question: From the top of a 15 m building the angle of elevation of the top of a taller building is 30 degrees and the angle of depression of its foot is 60 degrees. How tall is the taller building?
why: Distance = 15/tan 60 = 5 root 3. The taller building rises 5 root 3 x tan 30 = 5 m above the first, so its height is 15 + 5 = 20 m.

question: A car moves at constant speed towards a tower. The angle of elevation of the top changes from 30 degrees to 60 degrees in 12 seconds. How much longer will the car take to reach the foot of the tower?
why: Distances are h root 3 and h/root 3, so 12 s covers 2h/root 3. The remaining h/root 3 is half of that, so 6 s.

question: An aeroplane flies horizontally at height 1500 root 3 m. Its angle of elevation from a point on the ground changes from 60 to 30 degrees in 15 seconds. What is its speed?
why: Horizontal distance = 1500 root 3 (cot 30 - cot 60) = 3000 m in 15 s, which is 200 m/s = 720 km/h.

question: A flagstaff is fixed on top of a tower. From a point 30 m from the foot of the tower, the angle of elevation of the tower top is 30 degrees and of the flagstaff top is 45 degrees. How long is the flagstaff?
why: Top of flagstaff is at 30 tan 45 = 30 m. Flagstaff = 30 - 10 root 3 = 10(3 - root 3).

question: From two points 16 m and 36 m from the foot of a tower, on the same straight line, the angles of elevation of its top are complementary. How tall is the tower?
why: tan A = h/16 and tan(90 - A) = h/36. The product is 1, so h^2 = 576 and h = 24.

question: From the top of a 75 m lighthouse the angles of depression of two ships on opposite sides, in line with the base, are 30 and 45 degrees. How far apart are the ships?
why: Distances are 75 cot 30 = 75 root 3 and 75 cot 45 = 75. Total = 75(root 3 + 1).

question: A balloon is seen at 45 degrees elevation. After it rises 50 m vertically, it is seen at 60 degrees. What was its original height?
why: Horizontal distance d = h. Then h + 50 = h root 3, so h = 50/(root 3 - 1) = 25(root 3 + 1).

question: A man 1.5 m tall stands before a 31.5 m tower. The angle of elevation of the tower top from his eyes is 30 degrees. How far must he walk towards the tower to make it 45 degrees?
why: Height above eye level = 30 m. Distances are 30 root 3 and 30. He walks 30(root 3 - 1).

question: A 3 m tall statue stands on a pedestal. From a point on the ground the angle of elevation of the statue top is 60 degrees and of the pedestal top is 45 degrees. How high is the pedestal?
why: Let pedestal height h; distance d = h. Then h + 3 = h root 3, so h = 3/(root 3 - 1) = 3(root 3 + 1)/2.

question: A point P is 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. What is the length of a tangent from P to the circle?
why: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius, so length = root(13^2 - 5^2) = 12 cm.

question: What is the angle between a tangent to a circle and the radius through the point of contact?

question: A tangent to a circle of radius 6 cm has length 8 cm from an external point P. How far is P from the centre?

question: Two concentric circles have radii 13 cm and 5 cm. What is the length of the chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller circle?

question: A circle is inscribed in a right triangle with sides 6, 8 and 10 cm. What is its radius?

question: A quadrilateral ABCD circumscribes a circle with AB = 10, CD = 7 and BC = 9. What is AD?

question: PQ is a tangent at Q to a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm. If OP = 10 cm, what is the area of triangle OPQ?
why: PQ = 8 cm, and the right angle is at Q. Area = 1/2 x 6 x 8 = 24.

question: The distance of a point Q from the centre of a circle is 25 cm and the tangent from Q is 24 cm long. What is the radius?
why: Radius = root(25^2 - 24^2) = root 49 = 7 cm.

question: Tangents at A and B (the ends of a diameter) are parallel. A third tangent at C meets them at P and Q with AP = 5 cm and BQ = 7 cm. What is PQ?
why: Tangent lengths from P are equal, so PC = 5, and from Q, QC = 7. PQ = 5 + 7 = 12 cm.

question: A circle touches the sides of triangle ABC with AB = 12, BC = 10 and CA = 8 cm. What is the length of the tangent from A?

question: Tangents from P touch a circle of radius 6 cm at A and B, and angle APB = 60 degrees. What is PA?
why: OP bisects angle APB, so angle APO = 30 degrees. tan 30 = 6/PA gives PA = 6 root 3 cm.

question: A circle has radius 5 cm and a chord AB of length 8 cm. Tangents at A and B meet at P. What is PA?
why: The distance from O to AB is 3. OP = r^2/3 = 25/3. PA^2 = OP^2 - 25 = 400/9, so PA = 20/3.

question: A circle of radius 3 cm touches side BC of triangle ABC at D, with BD = 6 cm and DC = 9 cm. What is AC?
why: Let the tangent from A be x. The sides are x + 6, x + 9 and 15. Area = 3s and by Heron this gives x = 3, so AC = 12 cm.

question: Two circles of radii 4 cm and 9 cm touch externally. What is the length of a direct common tangent?
why: Length = 2 root(r1 x r2) = 2 root 36 = 12 cm.

question: What is the radius of the circle inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side 12 cm?
why: The altitude is 6 root 3 and the inradius is one-third of it: 2 root 3 cm.

question: Concentric circles have radii 5 cm and 3 cm. A chord AB of the larger circle touches the smaller one. What is the area of triangle OAB?
why: AB = 2 root(25 - 9) = 8 cm and the height from O is 3 cm. Area = 1/2 x 8 x 3 = 12.

question: Tangents PA and PB from P touch a circle at A and B, and angle APB = 40 degrees. What is angle PAB?

question: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is drawn into a wire of uniform circular cross-section of radius 0.2 cm. How long is the wire?

question: A cone is cut by a plane parallel to its base at half the height. What is the ratio of the volume of the small cone to that of the whole cone?

question: A tent is a cylinder of radius 7 m and height 6 m surmounted by a cone of height 24 m with the same radius. Canvas costs Rs 50 per square metre. What is the cost of canvas for the tent (no floor)? (Use pi = 22/7.)

question: Sand from a cylindrical bucket of radius 14 cm and height 18 cm is emptied to form a conical heap of height 24 cm. What is the radius of the heap?

question: A hemisphere of radius 7 cm of the largest possible size is placed on top of a cube of side 14 cm. What is the total surface area of the solid? (Use pi = 22/7.)

question: A solid is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end. Its total length is 24 cm and the diameter is 14 cm. What is its volume? (Use pi = 22/7.)

question: A solid sphere of radius 3.5 cm is completely dropped into a cylindrical vessel of radius 7 cm that holds water. By how much does the water level rise?

question: A solid cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 14 cm has a hemispherical hollow of radius 7 cm scooped out of its top. What is the total surface area of the remaining solid? (Use pi = 22/7.)

question: What is the class mark of the class interval 20 - 30?

question: For a grouped data the sum of f x (class mark) is 480 and the sum of frequencies is 24. What is the mean?

question: A table gives frequencies 5, 12 and 9 for classes 0-10, 10-20 and 20-30. What is the modal class?
why: The modal class is the class with the highest frequency, which is 10 - 20.

question: For grouped data with total frequency 50, which cumulative frequency value is used to find the median class?
why: The median class is the one whose cumulative frequency is just above N/2 = 25.

question: The mean of some data is 20 and the median is 21. Using the empirical formula, what is the mode?

question: A bag has 4 red, 5 black and 6 green balls. Two red balls are removed. A ball is then drawn at random. What is the probability that it is green?

question: A disc is chosen at random from discs numbered 1 to 90. What is the probability that it is a two-digit perfect square?
why: The two-digit squares up to 90 are 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81: six of them. P = 6/90 = 1/15.

question: A bag has 4 red balls and some blue balls. When 6 more blue balls are added, the probability of drawing blue doubles. How many blue balls were there at first?
why: (x + 6)/(x + 10) = 2x/(x + 4) gives x^2 + 10x - 24 = 0, so x = 2 (the root -12 is rejected).
